messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Arjun Singh <arjun@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo  Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Hi Arjun  thanks again for the demo time earlier. Putting the performance / SLO notes in one place so we have clear next steps. Please review and confirm or add any missing items.

Summary of targets discussed (please confirm):
- Latency: interactive chat (streaming) p95 <= 120 ms; p99 <= 300 ms.
- Throughput: sustained baseline 800 req/s (payloads avg ~350 tokens), burst capacity to 1,200 req/s for up to 2 minutes.
- Concurrency: support 200 concurrent websocket streams with per-connection KV cache enabled.
- Streaming: required  partial tokens must be delivered as they are generated (server-sent events/websocket).
- Token sizing: typical requests 150500 tokens in, 40200 tokens out; we should test at 500 in / 200 out to be safe.
- SLA expectations: 99.9% availability for the inference endpoint during pilot window; SLO penalty/escrow to be discussed later.

Assumptions to validate:
- Model: you indicated using open-model-x (7B fine-tuned) with float16 / q4_0 quantization. Confirm model name/version and any custom LLM hooks.
- Network: calls originate from FintechCo app region us-west-2; egress + inter-region latency needs to be measured.
- Warm KV cache for common prefixes expected for 60s TTL.

Proposed immediate next steps (MAP items):
1) FintechCo: share test harness + a representative workload (we'll use your staging keys).
2) Redwood: run a perf test with streaming enabled at 800/1,200 req/s and token mixes (target date: 2027-06-30).
3) Redwood: share raw perf logs, resource utilization, and a filled SLO checklist.
4) Decide: if p95 <= 150ms @ 800 req/s with streaming + acceptable cost profile -> pilot kickoff (Dedicated trial).

Attachments: fintechco_slo_checklist.xlsx (please fill any fields we missed).

Please confirm the targets above and any other decision criteria you care about (e.g., max cost per 1M tokens, burst duration). Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: FintechCo  Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Marissa  thanks, this is great and captures it well. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirming model: open-model-x v1.2 (we're running it quantized q4_0 on our current infra).
- Streaming: yes, streaming is mandatory for the primary chat flow (we rely on partial token display).
- Throughput: baseline 800 req/s is correct. We can tolerate 1,200 req/s bursts but only for ~90120s.
- Concurrency: 200 concurrent streams is accurate.
- Cost threshold: our platform team is targeting <= $6k per 1M output tokens (we know this is a rough number; open to negotiation if performance is strong).

Attached is a filled-first-pass of your SLO checklist  see column notes. We also attached a small synthetic harness (script + sample payloads) in the Drive link.

We'd like Redwood to run an initial perf test targeted at:
- 800 req/s sustained for 10 minutes (token mix: 500/200)
- Burst to 1,200 req/s for 2 minutes
- Streaming enabled
- Report p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, and network (egress/ingress) metrics

If results look good, our decision criteria lead is: meet latency targets OR show clear, documented mitigations (e.g., Dedicated pool sizing, prefix caching) and an acceptable cost estimate.

Thanks  I attached the SLO checklist as fintechco_slo_checklist.xlsx and linked the harness: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PerfTestDocs

Arjun
Arjun Singh

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 13:17:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: FintechCo  Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Marissa / Marcus  looping in some quick engineering notes and proposed test plan.

Notes:
- Streaming: Redwood runtime supports SSE/websocket streaming with efficient token flush; we need to confirm client-side ack expectations for partial tokens (Arjun to confirm if they expect ordering guarantees beyond per-connection).
- Model: q4_0 quantization of open-model-x is common; perf will vary based on KV cache hit rate and request seq length. We'll test with both cold and warm KV cache (warm = pre-populated prefixes).
- Network: because calls originate in us-west-2, we'll run tests from a us-west-2 probe to minimize inter-region noise.

Proposed perf test plan (engineer-run):
1) Baseline run: 800 req/s sustained for 10m, token mix 500in/200out, streaming enabled. Capture p50/p95/p99 and GPU utilization.
2) Burst run: ramp to 1,200 req/s for 2m, observe tail latencies and any queueing.
3) Cold vs Warm: repeat baseline with cold KV cache (no prefix) and warm (60s TTL).
4) Concurrency stress: open 200 concurrent websocket streams for 10m at 1 req/min each to emulate many keep-alive connections.

Outputs we'll provide: raw metrics (CSV), perf dashboard link, recommended Dedicated pool sizing and an estimated monthly cost delta.

Questions for Arjun (please confirm): model exact version (open-model-x v1.2 confirmed?) and whether you can provide traffic replay or we should use synthetic harness. Also confirm whether the app enforces TLS client certs as we may need an allowlist for perf probes.

I'll target running the first baseline on 2027-06-30 and will update the MAP with timestamps once I have the harness.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra

Arjun  thanks for the quick confirmation and the checklist  received. Quick decision-criteria recap so we're aligned on next steps:

Decision criteria for pilot approval:
- Latency: p95 <= 150ms at 800 req/s (streaming enabled) OR documented mitigation + Dedicated sizing that meets application SLAs.
- Throughput/Concurrency: stable 800 req/s with bursts to 1,200 req/s for 120s and support for 200 concurrent streams.
- Cost: preliminary estimate within ~20% of your $6k / 1M output token target (we'll provide a detailed estimate post-test).

If Redwood's perf run on 2027-06-30 meets the criteria above we'll move to pilot (Dedicated trial) and kick off procurement steps.
